  followed by an attribute on the next line. This is a small grammar

> Written by Claude Code (an AI agent) working under Rod's direction; Rod
> reviews before anything goes upstream.

Rust moves from the grammar bundled with go-tree-sitter to a vendored
tree-sitter-rust v0.24.2, built with the tool from #2. Stacked on #3.

## How it was made

```sh
go run ./cmd/grammar-refresh -lang rust \
  -url https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-rust -ref v0.24.2 -generate
```

v0.24.2 ships only ABI 15, so the tool resolved `tree-sitter-cli@latest` to
0.27.2, generated at `--abi 14`, and recorded both in the manifest. The
resulting `parser.c` is byte-identical to an earlier manual regeneration
with 0.26.7, which is mildly reassuring about generator drift.

## What changes

- `internal/sem/grammars/rust`: vendored sources plus a `binding.go`;
  `parser.go` imports it instead of `smacker/go-tree-sitter/rust`.
- `IdentityRevision` goes to 8 so cached snapshots rebuild. The goldens
  change only in that stamp, including `rust-basic` and `rust-oo`.
- `NOTICES` gains the grammar's MIT licence; `CHANGELOG` notes the switch.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/sem/` passes, including the Rust tests and
  `maskRustUnsupportedSyntax`, which stays.
- An earlier local benchmark (not re-run here, so treat as indicative)
  saw failing Rust files drop from 4,546 to 3,778 across 10 repos with
  v0.24.2.

Yes, there is some degradation, but it's narrow: it only affects files that already failed to parse. No file that parsed cleanly before loses anything. I ran both of Tom's comparisons over the ten lock-pinned Rust repositories (40,518 `.rs` files). Before is layer 2, which uses go-tree-sitter's bundled Rust grammar; after is layer 3, with the vendored v0.24.2.

**Per-file parser audit:**

| | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Files with parse errors | 4,332 | 3,562 |
| Symbols | 386,284 | 386,184 |

- **Fixed:** 772 files go from error to clean, mostly in `rust-lang/rust` (723 fewer errors) and Deno (52 → 6).
- **No regressions in clean files:** none of the files that parsed cleanly before loses a symbol.

**Where it degrades** (all in `rust-lang/rust`):

- **Worse error recovery in already-broken files:** 36 files that fail under both grammars lose 156 symbols on net. 17 of them use unstable const-trait syntax (`[const] Trait`), which neither grammar supports. The biggest losses:
  - `library/core/src/cmp.rs`: 39 symbols
  - `rustc_hir/.../diagnostic.rs`: 19 symbols
  - `tests/ui/unpretty/exhaustive.rs`: 16 symbols
  - `library/core/src/slice/cmp.rs`: 8 symbols
- **Two files newly fail to parse**, and both keep their one symbol:
  - `tests/crashes/132126.rs` is a deliberately broken known-bug fixture.
  - `tests/ui/parser/shebang/multiline-attrib.rs` is valid Rust, a `#!` line followed by an attribute. This one is a genuine small grammar regression.
- **Unexplained case:** I don't know why `diagnostic.rs` loses its 19 symbols. I ruled out my first guess (a trailing `\` in a doc comment) with a minimal reproduction, and stopped there rather than guess further.

**Whole-repository `graph-bench`:**

| | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Parse failures | 4,546 | 3,778 |
| Relations | 1,760,243 | 1,760,507 |

Those parse-failure numbers exactly match your earlier experiment. Eight repositories are unchanged. Deno gains 8 symbols and 750 relations. `rust-lang/rust` loses 108 symbols and 486 relations, which fits the already-failing files above.

**What changed in the PRs:**

- The write-up is committed as `internal/sem/grammars/rust/VALIDATION.md` on layer 3 and pushed.
- PR #4's description now cites these numbers, including the cost, instead of the old "indicative" line.
- I deleted the throwaway audit test before committing. The scripts and raw results are in `/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-rod-build-entire-graph/25be978d-7a70-4adc-9b09-1bae9ecaf35c/scratchpad/rust-val/`, if you'd like to dig into any file.

Rust moves from the grammar bundled with go-tree-sitter to a vendored
tree-sitter-rust v0.24.2, built with the tool from #2. Stacked on #3.

## How it was made

```sh
go run ./cmd/grammar-refresh -lang rust \
  -url https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-rust -ref v0.24.2 -generate
```

v0.24.2 ships only ABI 15, so the tool resolved `tree-sitter-cli@latest` to
0.27.2, generated at `--abi 14`, and recorded both in the manifest. The
resulting `parser.c` is byte-identical to an earlier manual regeneration
with 0.26.7, which is mildly reassuring about generator drift.

## What changes

- `internal/sem/grammars/rust`: vendored sources plus a `binding.go`;
  `parser.go` imports it instead of `smacker/go-tree-sitter/rust`.
- `IdentityRevision` goes to 8 so cached snapshots rebuild. The goldens
  change only in that stamp, including `rust-basic` and `rust-oo`.
- `NOTICES` gains the grammar's MIT licence; `CHANGELOG` notes the switch.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/sem/` passes, including the Rust tests and
  `maskRustUnsupportedSyntax`, which stays.
- [VALIDATION.md](internal/sem/grammars/rust/VALIDATION.md) has the
  per-file audit and graph-bench comparison over the ten lock-pinned Rust
  repos. Rust parse errors fall from 4,332 to 3,562 files, and no file that
  parsed cleanly before loses a symbol.
- The upgrade does cost something: 36 `rust-lang/rust` files that fail on
  both grammars recover worse, losing 156 symbols on net (about half use
  unstable const-trait syntax), and one valid fixture, a `#!` line followed
  by an attribute, newly fails. Whole-repo, `rust-lang/rust` loses 108
  symbols and 486 relations; Deno gains 8 and 750.

I've updated PR #4's description, and yes: the upgrade fixes the problem Thomas reported.

**His issue:** Thomas commented on #345 on 30 October. Rust files that use raw borrows (`&raw const x` and `&raw mut x`, stable since Rust 1.82) get `E_PARSE_ERROR`, because the bundled grammar is from August 2024. He suggested `grammar-refresh` as the fix once #357 landed.

**What I tested:** his reproduction, a `&raw mut` variant, his `addr_of!` control, and a caller function, run under both grammars:

| | Bundled grammar | v0.24.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `&raw const info` | parse error | clean |
| `&raw mut info` | parse error | clean |
| `addr_of!(info)` (control) | clean | clean |
| `neighbors` completeness line | `partial E_PARSE_ERROR`, 1 of 4 Rust files failed | 0 of 4 failed |

The last row compares your installed `entire graph` (`v0.6.1-nightly`) with a binary built from layer 3. I ran it on a temporary file in the worktree, which I've since deleted.

**One nuance:** Thomas said Graph couldn't list callers in such a file. In my small reproduction, the old build still found the caller by recovering what it could from the broken parse, and just flagged the file as partial. What the upgrade removes is the parse error itself. In larger files, that recovery would often lose more, which fits his symptom. I've put this caveat in the PR description too.

**PR description:** it now opens with a "Why" section that links his comment and includes that table. It names him as "Thomas", with no @-mention. The rest (how it was made, what changed, the validation numbers and their cost) is unchanged.

**Heads-up:** a link from a PR body to an upstream issue normally shows up on that issue's timeline as "mentioned this". So #345 may now show a reference to your fork's PR #4. Say if you'd rather I remove the link.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
> Written by Claude Code (an AI agent) working under Rod's direction; Rod
> reviews before anything goes upstream.

`grammar-refresh` can now build a grammar instead of only copying upstream's
generated files. That covers Tom's Swift compatibility patch, and the
growing list of grammars whose releases ship only ABI 15 (C# v0.23.5, Rust
v0.24.2).

This is the bottom of a three-PR stack: F# moves onto a patch in #3, and #4
uses the tool to vendor Rust v0.24.2.

## What changes

- A manifest entry can carry a `local_build` block:

  ```json
  "local_build": {
    "patch": "swift/compatibility.patch",
    "tree_sitter_cli": "0.24.7",
    "generate_args": ["--abi", "14"]
  }
  ```

- The tool applies `patch` to the fetched checkout with `git apply`, then
  runs `npx --yes tree-sitter-cli@<version> generate <args>`, then vendors
  as before. A failure at any step leaves the vendored folder and manifest
  untouched.
- Regenerating the recorded revision reuses the recorded CLI version, so it
  is reproducible. A new revision uses `@latest`, resolved once to an exact
  version, which is recorded. `-generate` adds the block to a new grammar,
  and `-tree-sitter-cli` pins a version.
- The ABI comes from one constant (`maxABI`), and a test fails if
  go-tree-sitter's `api.h` range ever stops matching it, so a runtime
  upgrade changes one value.
- Swift and C# now use `local_build`. Swift also picks up 0.24.7's
  generated `alloc.h` and `array.h` in place of upstream's committed copies
  (parameter names and MSVC pragma push/pop only; no parse change).

## Validation

- Regenerating Swift and C# at their recorded revisions with the real tool
  reproduces the vendored folders byte for byte.
- `mise run check`: everything passes except the known
  `internal/cli` exact-name search tests, which time out at 30 minutes
  under `-race` on `main` too. `internal/cli` passes in full without
  `-race` (319s).
- This is the first CI run on Windows for these tests, which now replace
  the `npx` runner in-process rather than relying on `PATH`.

## Worth knowing

- Generating needs Node.js (`npx`). Building or running Graph still never
  downloads or generates anything.
- tree-sitter can still generate ABI 14 today, but a future release may
  drop it. The error then suggests `-tree-sitter-cli <older version>`.

> Written by Claude Code (an AI agent) working under Rod's direction; Rod
> reviews before anything goes upstream.

Follow-up to [entireio/entire-graph#357](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/357),
which added `grammar-refresh` and vendored Swift 0.7.4 with Tom's
compatibility patch. That patch was reapplied by hand; this makes the tool
do it.

`grammar-refresh` can now build a grammar instead of only copying upstream's
generated files. That covers Tom's Swift compatibility patch, and the
growing list of grammars whose releases ship only ABI 15 (C# v0.23.5, Rust
v0.24.2).

This is the bottom of a three-PR stack: F# moves onto a patch in #3, and #4
uses the tool to vendor Rust v0.24.2.

## What changes

- A manifest entry can carry a `local_build` block:

  ```json
  "local_build": {
    "patch": "swift/compatibility.patch",
    "tree_sitter_cli": "0.24.7",
    "generate_args": ["--abi", "14"]
  }
  ```

- The tool applies `patch` to the fetched checkout with `git apply`, then
  runs `npx --yes tree-sitter-cli@<version> generate <args>`, then vendors
  as before. A failure at any step leaves the vendored folder and manifest
  untouched.
- Regenerating the recorded revision reuses the recorded CLI version, so it
  is reproducible. A new revision uses `@latest`, resolved once to an exact
  version, which is recorded. `-generate` adds the block to a new grammar,
  and `-tree-sitter-cli` pins a version.
- The ABI comes from one constant (`maxABI`), and a test fails if
  go-tree-sitter's `api.h` range ever stops matching it, so a runtime
  upgrade changes one value.
- Swift and C# now use `local_build`. Swift also picks up 0.24.7's
  generated `alloc.h` and `array.h` in place of upstream's committed copies
  (parameter names and MSVC pragma push/pop only; no parse change).

## Validation

- Regenerating Swift and C# at their recorded revisions with the real tool
  reproduces the vendored folders byte for byte.
- `mise run check`: everything passes except the known
  `internal/cli` exact-name search tests, which time out at 30 minutes
  under `-race` on `main` too. `internal/cli` passes in full without
  `-race` (319s).
- This is the first CI run on Windows for these tests, which now replace
  the `npx` runner in-process rather than relying on `PATH`.

## Worth knowing

- Generating needs Node.js (`npx`). Building or running Graph still never
  downloads or generates anything.
- tree-sitter can still generate ABI 14 today, but a future release may
  drop it. The error then suggests `-tree-sitter-cli <older version>`.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Starting point:** Rod's Swift grammar PR, entireio/entire-graph#357, was merged. A maintainer, Tom (Thomas Dohmke), had added a Swift `compatibility.patch` that is applied before regeneration. Rod asked to brainstorm extending `cmd/grammar-refresh` so it applies manifest patches and regenerates grammars, including grammars whose releases ship only ABI 15.
   - **Test cases:** (1) apply the Swift patch to a clean upstream copy and reproduce the vendored files; (2) build and vendor tree-sitter-rust v0.24.2.
   - **Original constraint:** "We shouldn't commit any grammar changes on this branch". This was later superseded: Rod asked for the Swift headers to be committed, and for layer 3 to commit Rust.
   - **Decisions Rod made:**
     - Fetch the tree-sitter-cli version through `npx` (option C).
     - Manifest `local_build` block with patch, CLI version and arguments.
     - Use `@latest` for a new ref and record the version; pin the version only when regenerating the same revision.
     - Document the Node requirement and the `@latest`/ABI 14 risk.
     - Don't worry about safe-chain.
     - Use approach A (extend the Go tool in place).
     - Execute "native" (inline, one fresh reviewer at the end).
   - **Stack:** Rod asked for a gh-stack: L1 the tool, L2 F# onto a patch with `local_changes` removed, L3 the Rust upgrade. The PRs are stacked in his fork.
   - **Later requests:**
     - Commit the generated Swift headers.
     - F# as a straight patch.
     - Define the max ABI in one place.
     - Record the F# CLI version for regeneration, with no F# upgrade, and reword the note to say the revision was *chosen* as the last ABI-14 generation but can now be upgraded and regenerated.
     - Open draft PRs in the fork.
     - Run Rust benchmarks before and after, in the style of `swift/VALIDATION.md`, and note any degraded files.
     - Cite Thomas's #345 comment in PR #4 and confirm the upgrade fixes his problem.
     - Mark PR #2 as a follow-up to #357.
     - Open an upstream draft PR for layer 1, linking the fork PRs for layers 2 and 3.
     - End the session.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Runtime and generator:** tree-sitter ABI 13–14 (the go-tree-sitter runtime range), and `tree-sitter generate --abi 14` via `npx --yes tree-sitter-cli@<v>`.
   - **Patching:** `git apply --directory=<subdir>`; patch paths are relative to the grammar directory.
   - **Manifest:** `internal/sem/grammars/grammars.json`; `IdentityRevision` in `internal/sem/provider.go`; golden fixtures regenerated with `-update`; `NOTICES` regenerated with `scripts/gen-notices.sh`.
   - **lazy-fetch guard test:** `internal/gitutil/lazy_fetch_guard_test.go` allows `exec` only in `cmd/grammar-refresh/main.go`.
   - **gh-stack:** `init`, `add`, `down`, `top`, `rebase --upstack --remote fork`, `push --remote fork`, and `submit --auto --remote fork` with `GH_REPO=rodbegbie/entire-graph`.
   - **Remotes:** `fork` is `rodbegbie/entire-graph` on GitHub; `origin` is the `entire://` mirror.
   - **Worktree:** `.claude/worktrees/grammar-refresh-local-build`. Its guard rejects complex shell, heredocs containing git-like text, and git commands outside the worktree.

3. Files and Code Sections (final state):
   - **`cmd/grammar-refresh/main.go`:**
     - `options` struct: `{Lang, Ref, URL, Subdir, ManifestPath, GrammarsDir string; Generate bool; TreeSitterCLI string}`. `AllowLocalChanges` was removed in L2.
     - Flags: `-generate` and `-tree-sitter-cli`.
     - `refresh(o options)`: validates `local_build.patch` with `filepath.IsLocal`, calls `findNPX()` before fetching when generating, fetches into a temp checkout, runs `applyPatch`, `resolveCLI`, `generate`, then `vendor`. An `abiError` hint reads "tree-sitter-cli %s may no longer generate ABI %d, so pass -tree-sitter-cli <older version>".
     - `applyPatch(checkout, subdir, patchFile)` runs `git apply --directory=`.
     - `var npx = runNPX`, `var findNPX` (`exec.LookPath`), and `errNoNPX = "tree-sitter generation needs Node.js; npx was not found on PATH"`.
     - The usage comment documents `minABI`/`maxABI`, `local_build` and `-generate`.
   - **`cmd/grammar-refresh/refresh.go`:**
     - `const minABI = 13; maxABI = 14` (the one place to edit), with a comment pointing to `TestABIRangeMatchesRuntime`.
     - `Grammar` has `Note` and `LocalBuild *LocalBuild` (`json:"local_build,omitempty"`); `LocalChanges` was removed.
     - `type LocalBuild struct {Patch, TreeSitterCLI string; GenerateArgs []string}`.
     - `abiError{abi}` keeps the original message text, with `--abi %d` derived from `maxABI`.
   - **`cmd/grammar-refresh/generate.go`:**
     - `defaultGenerateArgs = []string{"--abi", strconv.Itoa(maxABI)}`.
     - `wantsGeneration`; `cliVersion(existing, revision, o)` (override first, then the recorded version for the same revision, else `latest`); `generateArgs`.
     - `resolveCLI(dir, spec)` matches the regex `\b\d+\.\d+\.\d+\b`.
     - `generate(...)`'s error includes "if this release cannot generate ABI %d, pass -tree-sitter-cli <older version>".
   - **Tests:**
     - `patch_test.go`: patch applies, subdirectory patch, failure leaves files untouched, unsafe patch path rejected.
     - `generate_test.go`: an in-process `fakeNPX` that swaps `npx` and `findNPX`, plus tests for `TestCLIVersion`, the pinned version, `@latest` being recorded, no npx (`PATH` empty), generate failure leaving files untouched, the ABI 15 hint, the generate-failure hint, and an unparseable version.
     - `abi_test.go`: `TestABIRangeMatchesRuntime` reads go-tree-sitter's `api.h` via `go/build`.
     - `refresh_test.go`: call sites use `options{}`; `notedManifest` and `TestRefreshKeepsNoteAcrossRevisions` are adapted; `TestRefreshRefusesLocalChanges` was removed.
   - **`grammars.json`:**
     - Swift: `local_build {patch: swift/compatibility.patch, tree_sitter_cli: 0.24.7, --abi 14}`, no `local_changes`.
     - C#: `local_build {0.24.7, --abi 14}`.
     - F# (L2): `local_build {patch: fsharp/scanner-header.patch, tree_sitter_cli: 0.24.6, --abi 14}`, with a note that the revision was chosen as the last ABI-14 generation and can now be upgraded and regenerated.
     - Rust (L3): v0.24.2, revision 77a3747, `tree_sitter_cli: 0.27.2`.
   - **Docs and grammar files:**
     - `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `swift/README.md`: describe the build steps and Node, and say the output is reproduced exactly.
     - `swift/tree_sitter/alloc.h` and `array.h`: re-vendored from the 0.24.7 generator.
     - `fsharp/scanner-header.patch`: 775 lines; adds `src/scanner.h` and rewrites the include in `scanner.c`.
     - `internal/sem/grammars/rust/*`: vendored files, `binding.go` and `VALIDATION.md`.
     - `parser.go`: imports the vendored `rust`.
     - `provider.go`: `IdentityRevision` is "8", with a "Revision 8" comment; `identity_revision_test.go` expects "8"; 29 goldens are stamp-only changes; `NOTICES` and `CHANGELOG` updated.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Worktree guard rejected complex commands:** used Write/Edit and simple separate commands, and a scratch shell script for multi-step runs.
   - **lazy-fetch guard failed on `exec` in `refresh.go`:** moved process launches into `main.go`.
   - **Full `mise run check` timed out:** `internal/cli` `TestAgentSearchExactName*` exceed 30 minutes under `-race`. This also happens on `main`. The package passes without `-race` (319s).
   - **Reviewer Critical, Windows CI:** the shell-script fake `npx` on `PATH` wouldn't work on Windows. Fixed with in-process swappable vars.
   - **Reviewer Important:** added the hint to generate failures, and corrected the docs that overclaimed reproduction.
   - **Swift regeneration differed in `alloc.h`/`array.h`:** Rod chose to commit the generated headers.
   - **`gh stack rebase` failed on multiple remotes:** added `--remote fork`.
   - **Wrong SHA tail in `VALIDATION.md`:** corrected to `e5e03947b70447f790a6c8a20df067643b1bd9cd`.
   - **`gh pr create` upstream failed:** "Resource not accessible by personal access token". Rod opened the upstream PR manually.
   - **First `diagnostic.rs` hypothesis was wrong:** a trailing `\` in a doc comment was ruled out with a reproduction. The cause remains unidentified.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Reproducibility:** Swift and C# rebuild byte for byte. F# with 0.24.6 plus the patch rebuilds byte for byte. Rust from 0.27.2 is identical to the 0.26.7 build. F# 0.3.12 also builds, but wasn't adopted.
   - **Rust per-file audit:** 40,518 files; parse errors fall from 4,332 to 3,562; 772 files fixed and 2 newly failing (`tests/crashes/132126.rs`, and `tests/ui/parser/shebang/multiline-attrib.rs`, which is valid Rust). No clean file loses symbols. 36 already-failing `rust-lang/rust` files lose 156 symbols on net; 17 of those involve const-trait syntax.
   - **Rust graph-bench:** parse failures fall from 4,546 to 3,778; relations go from 1,760,243 to 1,760,507; `rust-lang/rust` changes by −108 symbols and −486 relations.
   - **Thomas's `&raw const` and `&raw mut` reproduction:** errors before, clean after; `neighbors` completeness goes from "1 of 4 failed" to "0 of 4".

6. All user messages:
   - Initial request: brainstorm `grammar-refresh` applying the patch and regenerating; Rod has `tree-sitter-cli` from Homebrew; the test cases are the Swift patch and Rust v0.24.2; "We shouldn't commit any grammar changes on this branch -- just validate that it works correctly."
   - "C. The manifest file could change local_changes to be a pointer to the patch file. Perhaps "local_changes" could be replaced by a local_generation field which maps to a dictionary of "tree-sitter-cli-version", "tree-sitter-cli-switches" and "patch-file"?"
   - "Let's not move F# now. That can be a follow-up. > Written by Claude Code (an AI agent) working under Rod's direction; Rod
> reviews before anything goes upstream.

Follow-up to [entireio/entire-graph#357](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/357),
which added `grammar-refresh` and vendored Swift 0.7.4 with Tom's
compatibility patch. That patch was reapplied by hand; this makes the tool
do it.

`grammar-refresh` can now build a grammar instead of only copying upstream's
generated files. That covers Tom's Swift compatibility patch, and the
growing list of grammars whose releases ship only ABI 15 (C# v0.23.5, Rust
v0.24.2).

This is the first of three stacked changes. The other two are previewed as
PRs in my fork and will follow once this one lands:

- [rodbegbie/entire-graph#3](https://github.com/rodbegbie/entire-graph/pull/3)
  moves F# onto a patch and removes `local_changes`.
- [rodbegbie/entire-graph#4](https://github.com/rodbegbie/entire-graph/pull/4)
  uses the tool to vendor Rust v0.24.2, which fixes the `&raw const` parse
  errors Thomas reported on #345.

## What changes

- A manifest entry can carry a `local_build` block:

  ```json
  "local_build": {
    "patch": "swift/compatibility.patch",
    "tree_sitter_cli": "0.24.7",
    "generate_args": ["--abi", "14"]
  }
  ```

- The tool applies `patch` to the fetched checkout with `git apply`, then
  runs `npx --yes tree-sitter-cli@<version> generate <args>`, then vendors
  as before. A failure at any step leaves the vendored folder and manifest
  untouched.
- Regenerating the recorded revision reuses the recorded CLI version, so it
  is reproducible. A new revision uses `@latest`, resolved once to an exact
  version, which is recorded. `-generate` adds the block to a new grammar,
  and `-tree-sitter-cli` pins a version.
- The ABI comes from one constant (`maxABI`), and a test fails if
  go-tree-sitter's `api.h` range ever stops matching it, so a runtime
  upgrade changes one value.
- Swift and C# now use `local_build`. Swift also picks up 0.24.7's
  generated `alloc.h` and `array.h` in place of upstream's committed copies
  (parameter names and MSVC pragma push/pop only; no parse change).

## Validation

- Regenerating Swift and C# at their recorded revisions with the real tool
  reproduces the vendored folders byte for byte.
- `mise run check`: everything passes except the known
  `internal/cli` exact-name search tests, which time out at 30 minutes
  under `-race` on `main` too. `internal/cli` passes in full without
  `-race` (319s).
- This is the first CI run on Windows for the new tests (the fork cannot
  use the Depot runners). They replace the `npx` runner in-process rather
  than relying on `PATH`, so they should not need Node or a shell there.

## Worth knowing

- Generating needs Node.js (`npx`). Building or running Graph still never
  downloads or generates anything.
- tree-sitter can still generate ABI 14 today, but a future release may
  drop it. The error then suggests `-tree-sitter-cli <older version>`.

> Written by Claude Code (an AI agent) working under Rod's direction; Rod
> reviews before anything goes upstream.

Rust moves from the grammar bundled with go-tree-sitter to a vendored
tree-sitter-rust v0.24.2, built with the tool from #2. Stacked on #3.

## Why

While the Swift grammar refresh was under way, Thomas pointed out on
[entireio/entire-graph#345](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/issues/345#issuecomment-6532737539)
that Rust has the same root cause. The bundled grammar (August 2024) predates
raw borrows, `&raw const x` and `&raw mut x`, which have been stable since
Rust 1.82. Any file that uses one gets `E_PARSE_ERROR`.

This fixes it. Using his reproduction, plus a `&raw mut` variant and a
caller:

| | Bundled grammar | v0.24.2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `&raw const info` | parse error | clean |
| `&raw mut info` | parse error | clean |
| `std::ptr::addr_of!(info)` (control) | clean | clean |
| `neighbors` completeness | `partial E_PARSE_ERROR`, 1 of 4 Rust files failed | 0 of 4 failed |

(In that small repro the old build still found the caller through partial
recovery; the parse error is what goes away.)

## How it was made

```sh
go run ./cmd/grammar-refresh -lang rust \
  -url https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-rust -ref v0.24.2 -generate
```

v0.24.2 ships only ABI 15, so the tool resolved `tree-sitter-cli@latest` to
0.27.2, generated at `--abi 14`, and recorded both in the manifest. The
resulting `parser.c` is byte-identical to an earlier manual regeneration
with 0.26.7, which is mildly reassuring about generator drift.

## What changes

- `internal/sem/grammars/rust`: vendored sources plus a `binding.go`;
  `parser.go` imports it instead of `smacker/go-tree-sitter/rust`.
- `IdentityRevision` goes to 8 so cached snapshots rebuild. The goldens
  change only in that stamp, including `rust-basic` and `rust-oo`.
- `NOTICES` gains the grammar's MIT licence; `CHANGELOG` notes the switch.

## Validation

- `go test ./internal/sem/` passes, including the Rust tests and
  `maskRustUnsupportedSyntax`, which stays.
- [VALIDATION.md](internal/sem/grammars/rust/VALIDATION.md) has the
  per-file audit and graph-bench comparison over the ten lock-pinned Rust
  repos. Rust parse errors fall from 4,332 to 3,562 files, and no file that
  parsed cleanly before loses a symbol.

# Rod's Professional Voice

Rod writes formal docs and casual Slack messages in the *same personality at different volumes*. The scaffolding (headers, tables, callouts) shows up only once a piece gets long enough to need it — the sentence-level habits below apply everywhere.

Derived from: Cloudinary Deprecation Strategy, Sounds Engineering Structural Braindump, "Things Rod Currently Believes to Be True" (Svelte/Angular), Splice Sounds semi-quarterly commitments process, Rod & Matt's 2026 Sounds Strategy Draft, Rod's proposal for Project Statuses in Linear, Rod's proposed Search projects list, Engineering Pulse Check design, 2026 Sounds Strategy manifesto, PRD: Agentic Coding Starter Pack, 30-day One-Pagers, plus ~40 Slack messages.

## Before drafting, calibrate the register

Ask: is this a **doc** (Notion strategy/process/PRD/DACI) or a **message** (Slack, quick update, comment)?

- **Docs** get the full structural toolkit in section 1.
- **Messages** skip headers/ToC/callouts but keep every voice habit in section 2 — hedging, specific numbers, dry parentheticals, credit-giving — plus the diction rules in section 3 and the Slack-specific notes (short punchy sign-offs, explicit rollback notes) in section 4.

If genuinely unsure which register fits, default to the lighter one — Rod's docs are notable for restraint, not for reaching for structure they don't need.

## 1. Structural signature (docs only)

Apply these in roughly this order when building a doc:

- **Open with the decision or belief, not the background.** DACIs open with "What decision needs to be made?" Proposals open with the ask, not the history.
- **Name Non-Goals explicitly, as their own section**, and make them do real work (pre-empt a specific likely misreading, not a generic disclaimer). E.g. "Velocity is seen as the arbiter of what plugins people can/should use" as an explicit non-goal.
- **Use hypothesis → prediction framing for anything proposing an experiment or bet**: "We believe X. Prediction: if we do Y, Z will happen." Follow with "What do you have to believe to endorse this plan?" for higher-stakes bets.
- **Bury detail in toggles, not in the main flow.** Meeting notes, edge cases, and "most readers can ignore this" content go under a `{toggle="true"}` block. Say explicitly that it's skippable.
- **Tables for anything comparative** — pricing, ownership, priority definitions. Put a number on things people usually leave vague (e.g. "85% of these projects should be delivered," not "most").
- **One callout box near the top** (💡, ℹ️, or ⭐ icon) giving the reader the one thing they need before the rest makes sense.
- **Table of contents on anything over ~800 words.**
- **Name your own rhetorical device when you use one**, with a link if there's a source: Cunningham's Law, DACI, Hofstadter's Law, Stepping Stones not Milestones, Strangler Fig, "5 So-Whats" (Rod's own remix of 5 Whys).
- **Close on one short sentence that reframes the whole doc** — not a summary paragraph. ("The best time to start was last year, the second best time is now!")

## 2. Voice habits (everywhere — docs and Slack)

- **Hedge visibly rather than assert past your actual knowledge.** "I currently believe, low confidence," "AFAICT," "I don't have a good sense right now," "I suspect." This is a feature, not a weakness — Rod's docs read as more credible because of it, not less.
- **Quantify instead of gesturing.** Not "a lot of the bill" — "58.5% of our AWS bill is now tagged." Not "search is broken sometimes" — "milestone rate is 20–30% per search."
- **Dry humour lives in parentheses, never in the topic sentence.** "(Or maybe not if we're moving the catalogue to a CMS?)" The main clause stays flat and informative; the joke is the aside.
- **Credit people by name, inline, even when driving the doc yourself.** "As Jenn pointed out..." / "@so-and-so, does anyone have context for...?"
- **Frame drafts as drafts, out loud, so nobody over-reads them.** "It's a strawman proposal — please don't read too much into just the words in this doc."
- **Blunt when the content calls for it, but never padded.** Direct critical assessments are delivered plainly, without corporate softening *and* without unnecessary harshness — state the observation, don't decorate it.
- **No swearing in anything shared, drafted, or sent.** It has appeared exactly once across the whole corpus, in the single most private, least-shared personal doc, used for emphasis rather than decoration. Default: never swear in output. If Rod explicitly asks for it in a specific throwaway/personal note, that's his call, not the default.

## 3. Diction

- British spelling throughout: organised, favour, recognise, licence (noun) — including in fast Slack messages, not just polished docs.
- Reach-for words: *cadence, friction, ladder up, shepherd, muscle (as in "build new muscle"), toil, papercuts, blast radius, force multiplier, boring technology, portfolio-based approach.*
- Coin a compact label for a recurring concept rather than using a generic noun: "Friction Shepherd," "Fresh Socks," "junk drawer team," "hyperobject flailing."
- Precise engineering/product jargon is fine and expected — this is written by and for engineers — but decorative jargon with no added precision is not Rod's style.

## 4. Slack-specific notes

- Short. Rarely more than a paragraph unless it's an incident/status update.
- Status and incident updates keep bullets even in Slack — e.g. a root-cause bullet, a fix bullet, a caveat bullet.
- Common sign-offs: "Thanks all!", "LMK if anyone sees issues," "Have a great weekend," "Happy break, friends!"
- Rollback/verification plans get stated explicitly and briefly even in a casual channel post: what changed, expected impact (usually "none"), how to flag a problem.
- Questions to the team are genuinely open, not rhetorical: "Does anyone ever use X?" rather than assuming the answer.

## 5. Quick self-check before sending

- [ ] Does the first sentence say the decision/ask/belief, not the throat-clearing?
- [ ] Is there at least one specific number instead of a vague quantifier?
- [ ] Is uncertainty flagged where it exists, rather than smoothed over?
- [ ] Is anyone else's contribution credited by name if relevant?
- [ ] Does it end on a line that lands, not a recap?
- [ ] No swearing, no unearned jargon, no corporate padding?

If drafting a long doc (>800 words), also check: ToC present, Non-Goals section present if scope could be misread, one framing callout near the top, detail pushed into toggles rather than inline.

# gh-stack

`gh stack` is a [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) extension for stacked branches and pull
requests. A stack is an ordered chain of branches rooted on a trunk, where each branch has one PR
based on the branch below it, so a reviewer sees only that layer's diff.

`gh stack` prints a stack trunk-first, left to right:

```
(main) <- auth <- api <- frontend
```

Left is the **bottom**, right is the **top**. `auth` is based on `main` and merges first;
`frontend` merges last. `up` moves toward the top, away from trunk; `down` moves toward it.
Foundational work belongs at the bottom, code that depends on it above. For how to choose the
layers, read `references/stack-design.md`.

## Setup

Requires Git 2.36+ and an authenticated GitHub CLI.

```bash
gh extension install github/gh-stack
git config rerere.enabled true         # remember conflict resolutions
git config remote.pushDefault origin   # required if the repo has more than one remote
```

## Non-interactive use

`gh stack` branches on whether **stdout is a TTY**. Piped, most commands error cleanly or print
static text; under a PTY the same commands open a prompt or a full-screen TUI and block forever.
Agent harnesses differ, so always pass the flags below instead of relying on that detection.

**Multiple remotes:** never run `push`, `submit`, `sync`, `rebase`, or `link` without
`--remote <name>` unless `remote.pushDefault` is configured. `checkout` and `trunk` have no
`--remote` flag and require the config.

| Always run | Never run bare | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `gh stack view --json` | `gh stack view` | opens a TUI under a PTY |
| `gh stack submit --auto` | `gh stack submit` | prompts for a title per new PR |
| `gh stack merge <target> --yes` | `gh pr merge` | `gh pr merge` cannot merge a stack |
| `gh stack init <branch>...` | `gh stack init` | prompts for branch names |
| `gh stack add <branch>` | `gh stack add` | prompts for a name, and fails even when piped |
| `gh stack checkout <target>` | `gh stack checkout` | opens a selection menu |
| `gh stack up` / `down` / `top` / `bottom` | `gh stack switch` | `switch` is menu-only |
| — | `gh stack modify` | TUI-only, no non-interactive path |

- `view --short` is safe in both modes, but it is formatted for humans. Use `--json` to parse.
- **`checkout <pr>` when a different local stack already covers those branches** cannot be forced.
  Run `gh stack unstack --local` first (this keeps the stack on GitHub), then retry.
- **Worktrees:** local stacks share one common-directory catalog. Use `--print-path` with
  navigation or explicit-target `checkout` to locate a foreign-owned branch without stealing its
  checkout. Unoccupied targets are checked out here first. Check the exit status before changing
  directories; parse only successful path-mode stdout, never status messages.

## Branch placement

- **Starting multi-part work:** create the stack before writing files. Do not implement every
  concern on trunk and split it later. Put one dependent concern in each layer, bottom to top.
- **Editing an existing stack:** check out the layer that owns the change before editing. Never
  commit a lower layer's concern on the current top branch. Run `gh stack view --json`; if
  ownership is unclear, inspect `git log --all -- <path>`. Then check out the owner, edit, commit,
  rebase upstack, and return to top.

```bash
gh stack down                   # or: gh stack checkout api
git add ... && git commit -m "Add get-user endpoint"
gh stack rebase --upstack       # replay every branch above onto the change
gh stack top                    # return to where you were
gh stack push
```

## Core loop

```bash
gh stack init auth              # create the stack and check out its branch
git add ... && git commit -m "Add auth middleware"
gh stack add api                # next layer, branched from the current one
git add ... && git commit -m "Add API routes"
gh stack submit --auto          # push every branch and open draft PRs
gh stack view --json            # confirm
```

Add `--open` to `submit` to create PRs ready for review instead of drafts. Branch names are
verbatim — `gh stack add refactor/foo` creates `refactor/foo`.

## Staying in sync

```bash
gh stack sync                   # fetch, reconcile with GitHub, rebase, push, refresh PR state
gh stack sync --prune           # also delete local branches for merged PRs
```

Pruning never happens without `--prune` when non-interactive. If the local and remote stacks have
diverged, `sync` prints both chains, makes no changes, and exits 0 with `Sync aborted` — see
`references/troubleshooting.md`.

## Merging

Scope the merge with an argument:

```bash
gh stack merge 42 --yes          # PR #42 plus every unmerged PR below it
gh stack merge 7 --yes           # every unmerged PR in stack #7
gh stack merge 42 --yes --squash # or --merge, --rebase, --merge-method <method>
```

Pass a PR number to merge that PR and every unmerged PR below it, or a stack number to merge every
unmerged PR in that stack. The operation is all-or-nothing: if any PR in that set cannot merge,
none do.

Without a method flag the last-used method is reused. If the base branch uses a merge queue, the
stack is queued instead and the queue picks the method, ignoring any flag you passed with a
warning; queued PRs may land in separate groups.

## Reading state

`gh stack view --json` writes JSON to **stdout**. Status messages go to **stderr** — do not parse
them, branch on exit codes instead.

```
trunk           string
currentBranch   string
branches[]      name, head, base, isCurrent, isMerged, isQueued, needsRebase
branches[].pr   number, url, state ("OPEN" | "MERGED" | "QUEUED"); absent when no PR exists
```

`base` is the saved SHA of the parent branch that this branch was last known to contain. It may be
older than the parent's current tip. `needsRebase` is true when the current parent tip is no longer
an ancestor of the branch.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Success | — |
| 1 | Generic error | Read stderr |
| 2 | Not in a stack | `gh stack init`, or `gh stack checkout <target>` |
| 3 | Rebase conflict | Follow the Exit 3 recovery below |
| 4 | GitHub API failure | Check `gh auth status`, retry |
| 5 | Invalid arguments | Fix the invocation; see `<command> --help` |
| 6 | Disambiguation required | Branch is in several stacks; check out a non-shared branch |
| 7 | Rebase already in progress | `gh stack rebase --continue` or `--abort` |
| 8 | Stack file locked | Another `gh stack` process is writing; retry after ~5s |
| 9 | Stacked PRs unavailable | Not enabled on the repository; tell the user |
| 10 | Modify recovery required | `gh stack modify --abort` |

**Exit 3 recovery:**

- After `gh stack rebase`: resolve the files, run `git add`, then
  `gh stack rebase --continue`; use `gh stack rebase --abort` to restore the stack.
- After `gh stack sync`: the stack has already been restored. Run `gh stack rebase` to recreate the
  conflict, then resolve and continue as above.

## Constraints

- Stacks are strictly linear: one parent, at most one child. Use separate stacks for parallel work.
- `rebase` and `sync` automatically update affected clean worktrees; they never auto-stash or
  create/remove worktrees. Mutations serialize across the clone, and paused operations require
  recovery in their recorded owners.
- `modify` supports distributed stack branches, but its editor remains TUI-only. Actions run in
  affected clean owners; unoccupied branches use the origin. Drop/fold source branches and
  worktrees are preserved. Recovery flags may run from any worktree and use recorded native
  operation owners; never resolve/stage in the caller's tree unless the diagnostic names it.
- There is no non-interactive reorder or removal. Errors may suggest `gh stack modify`, but it is
  TUI-only — restructure with `unstack` then `init` instead.
- PR titles and bodies are auto-generated. Use `gh pr edit` afterwards to change them.

## More detail

`gh stack <command> --help` is authoritative for flags and arguments. Note that
`gh stack help <command>` does **not** work — it prints the top-level help.

Open the reference whose trigger matches the task; no need to preload all three.

- `references/stack-design.md` — read before creating a stack, when deciding how many layers to
  use, what belongs in each one, or whether work belongs in a new stack.
- `references/commands.md` — read when a command fails unexpectedly or you need its preconditions,
  side effects, atomicity, or ordering guarantees.
- `references/troubleshooting.md` — read on a rebase conflict, after a squash-merge, on local and
  remote divergence, when restructuring a stack, or when driving stacks from another tool.
