## HEAD (no branch)
----
- **Vendored grammars** under `internal/sem/grammars` record their origin in
  `internal/sem/grammars/grammars.json`. Refresh one with
  `go run ./cmd/grammar-refresh -lang <name> -ref <tag|branch|commit>` (add
  `-url` for a new grammar); it needs the network, and its output is committed.
  The go-tree-sitter runtime loads ABI 13-14 only. An entry's `local_build`
  block makes the tool build the grammar instead of copying it: `patch` (a
  path under `internal/sem/grammars`) is applied to the checkout, then the
  parser is regenerated with
  `npx tree-sitter-cli@<tree_sitter_cli> generate <generate_args>`. Pass
  `-generate` to add that block to a grammar whose release ships only ABI 15;
  it defaults to `--abi 14`. Generating needs Node.js (`npx`) on `PATH`.
  Regenerating the recorded revision reuses the recorded CLI version, so the
  output matches the vendored files exactly. A new revision uses
  `tree-sitter-cli@latest` and records the version it ran. `-tree-sitter-cli
  <version>` overrides both. Tree-sitter can currently still generate ABI 14,
  but a future release may drop it. If the tool then reports an ABI it cannot
  vendor, pin an older CLI with `-tree-sitter-cli`. Any other difference from
  upstream belongs in the entry's patch, so a refresh never needs manual
  edits. Check the entry's `note`, regenerate
  `NOTICES`, and bump `IdentityRevision` in `internal/sem/provider.go` in the
  same commit when parse results change.
- **User-visible behavior** belongs in `CHANGELOG.md` under the unreleased
  section, grouped by Keep a Changelog heading. Tagged releases publish that
----

----

+++ b/internal/sem/text.go
+	suffix := fmt.Sprintf(" (%d dependents)", change.DependentsCount)
-		return " (1 dependent)"
+		suffix = " (1 dependent)"
-	return fmt.Sprintf(" (%d dependents)", change.DependentsCount)
+	// The dependents scan is always a heuristic (see dependentsEvidenceState); that alone
+	// stays silent here so an ordinary diff reads exactly as it always has. It only
+	// speaks up when the scan itself hit a real limit -- the count may be missing
+	// candidates entirely, not merely imprecise, and the reader needs to know to check.

content.text:
Your fork's `main` now matches upstream at `0e6bbba3`, and both branches are rebased locally but **not pushed**. F# is at `1dbc3fc4` and Rust at `47f4fa3a`. F# rebased cleanly. Rust only conflicted on its 29 goldens, because upstream's schema 1.5 and our `IdentityRevision` 8 edit the same line. I regenerated those, and they now differ from `main` only in that stamp.

## What #394 added
The extra commit and the merge were both by suhaanthayyil, and it makes three changes:
- **ABI no longer pinned:** the tool stops writing the default `--abi 14` into the manifest. Otherwise a future `maxABI` bump would leave every grammar generating the old ABI, and nothing would fail.
- **Prerelease CLI versions:** these are now recorded in full, rather than `0.25.0-rc.1` being recorded as `0.25.0`.
- **Patches that need generation:** a patch that touches `grammar.js` with no generator configured is now refused. It used to be silently lost.

The last two were on our deferred list, so those are now closed.

## Changes needed
1. **Remove `generate_args` from the F# and Rust manifest entries.** Both still carry the pin the new commit removes. Upstream's rule is that it stays only for args someone chose on purpose.
2. **Fix the baseline in `rust/VALIDATION.md`.** It cites `e5e03947`, which stops being reachable on your fork once we force-push. The measurements still hold, because upstream's `internal/sem` changes since then don't touch parsing. I'd describe the baseline as the bundled grammar and drop the SHA, which also survives any further rebases.
3. **Update the fork PRs.** #4's description says the tool "recorded both" the version and the args, and #3 and #4 refer to #2 as their base. #2 is effectively done now, so it should come out of the stack.
4. **Optional doc tweak:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` shows `generate <generate_args>` as if the field were always set. It could say that it's an optional override.

`IdentityRevision` 8 is still right, since `main` is on 7.

## Verification
- **Real rebuilds:** with `generate_args` removed, F#, Rust, Swift and C# all rebuilt byte for byte through real `npx`, and the manifest stayed free of the args.
- **The untested generation path:** the PR comment said 11 tests on this path couldn't run on their machine. They pass here as part of `cmd/grammar-refresh`.
- **Tests on each layer:** `cmd/grammar-refresh`, `internal/gitutil` and `internal/sem` all pass on both.
- **Not run:** `internal/cli`, `-race`, or the full `mise run check`. I also didn't check #394's Windows CI result.

## One thing that's unclear
The PR comment mentions a `vendoredGrammarsDigest` on a "#357 follow-ups branch". It isn't on `main`, and a search of open upstream PRs found nothing, though that search may not cover code in their diffs. If it lands, adding Rust's vendored files would probably change that digest, so whichever PR lands second would need updating.

Do you want me to make changes 1, 2 and 4 as fixups to the commits that own them, then force-push both branches and update the fork PRs? Your local `main` is still on the old commit, and I can fast-forward that too.

--- ashtom 2026-11-05T12:43:59Z
@rodbegbie Sounds good to me. Merging this one in the meantime.

--- rodbegbie 2026-11-07T23:09:04Z
> [@rodbegbie](https://github.com/rodbegbie) Sounds good to me. Merging this one in the meantime.

Hi Tom. I spent some time with Claude on this, and it’s now in PR #394.  I think this will improve the developer ergonomics for refreshing grammars quite a bit.

--- suhaanthayyil 2026-11-08T17:07:29Z
Follow-ups from reviewing this after merge are now pushed on `fix/357-followups` (nothing merged):

- `grammar-refresh` wrote more than one manifest entry per language, and deleted vendored files before writing the replacements, so a failure mid-copy left the folder partly emptied.
- It would silently pick between two candidate licence files.
- Nothing in the suite could notice a grammar change: there is no Swift fixture, and the one golden holding Swift symbols is byte-identical across the 0.5.0 → 0.7.4 swap apart from `identity_revision`. `TestVendoredGrammarBytesAreTiedToTheIdentityRevision` now pins the bytes of all 62 vendored grammar files, so a refresh forces a decision about `IdentityRevision` instead of passing quietly.

A method note for anyone adding tests over vendored files: `go test -overlay` replaces what the **compiler** reads, not what `os.ReadFile` reads at runtime. I "proved" the two new data-file tests could fail by overlaying a mutated `scanner.c` and `grammars.json`, and both mutations came back `ok`. Mutating in place and restoring with `git checkout --` turned all three red immediately.

The one claim in `VALIDATION.md` I could not reproduce — that applying `compatibility.patch` and generating with tree-sitter-cli 0.24.7 reproduces `parser.c` and `scanner.c` byte for byte — is exactly what #394 makes reproducible by building it in the tool. Reviewed there.

content.text:
That comment answers my question about the digest, and it comes from suhaanthayyil again. `fix/357-followups` is pushed but not merged, and I can't find a PR for it. Its digest test is meant to force a decision about `IdentityRevision` whenever a refresh changes grammar bytes.

**Effect on our branches:**
- **Rust:** adding the vendored Rust files will trip that test. We've already bumped `IdentityRevision` to 8, so whichever lands second just updates the digest constant.
- **F#:** this shouldn't be affected, because that layer isn't meant to change any vendored bytes. The running check confirms that.
- **Merge conflicts:** the branch merges cleanly with today's `main`, but conflicts with our stack in `cmd/grammar-refresh/main.go` and `refresh_test.go`. I haven't looked at those hunks yet, but F# removes `local_changes`, and the branch edits around it (including a warning line right next to its new code in `main.go`). Whichever lands second has to resolve that.

**The claim they couldn't reproduce:** they couldn't confirm that `compatibility.patch` plus tree-sitter-cli 0.24.7 reproduces Swift's `parser.c` and `scanner.c` byte for byte. Today's real rebuild did exactly that, with no differences in any vendored Swift file. That was on my machine through `npx`, but it does settle the claim, and it might be worth telling them. I won't post anything unless you ask.

Their `go test -overlay` warning doesn't affect us, because my digest check doesn't use overlays. That check is still running, and I'll report its results when it finishes, along with whether their new tests still compile against the `refresh(options{})` signature.

The digest check is done. The follow-ups branch needs rework against current `main` whether or not our stack lands, so I need to correct what I said earlier. It does merge cleanly with `main`, but only as text: **it won't compile**. Eight of its `refresh(...)` calls use the old positional arguments, and #394 changed that function to take `options{}`.

| Branch | Vendored files | Digest | Manifest test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 62 | `287bec77…` | passes |
| F# | 62 | `287bec77…` (unchanged) | passes |
| Rust | 68 | `6faff18a…` | passes |

Only the digest test fails on these three, because the branch still pins `769dfdcf…` from before #394. Both `main`'s digest and its 62 files match what they predicted in their #394 comment.

What that means for each side:
- **`fix/357-followups`:** it needs a rebase, the digest updated to `287bec77…`, and those eight calls rewritten. One of them, at line 460, passes `allowLocalChanges=true`, a flag that exists only until F# lands.
- **F#:** the digest isn't affected. If F# lands first, the follow-ups branch also has to drop its `local_changes` test and remove the old warning code in `main.go`.
- **Rust:** whichever lands second sets the digest. If nothing else changes the vendored grammars first, Rust's will be `6faff18a…`. `IdentityRevision` 8 already covers the decision that test forces.

None of this changes the list of fixes I gave you, so landing order is the only new question. I'd land F# and Rust first if suhaanthayyil is happy with that, since their branch needs rebasing anyway, and removing `local_changes` first means they won't write tests for a flag that's about to go. The downside is that it asks them to wait.

The worktree is clean and back on the Rust branch. Shall I go ahead with the fixups, the force-push and the fork PR updates?
